title: Brixton Emergency Help Points
summary: Emergency medical facilities, walk-in centres, hazards, and essential supplies in Brixton.
content:
For life-threatening emergencies, call 999 or 112 immediately.

1. 24-Hour Emergency Hospitals (A&E):
- King's College Hospital (Major Trauma Centre): Denmark Hill, SE5 9RS. From Brixton station: ~20-25 min walk east along Coldharbour Lane (approx 1.1 miles), or bus 35, 45, or 345 east directly to Denmark Hill / hospital gates.
- St Thomas' Hospital: Westminster Bridge Road, SE1 7EH. From Brixton station: bus 159 northbound along Brixton Road and Kennington Road (~25 min journey).

2. Urgent Treatment Centres:
- King's College Hospital Urgent Treatment Centre: Ground Floor, Denmark Hill, SE5 9RS (co-located beside main A&E entrance).

3. Local Hazards & Infrastructure:
- Effra River culverted flood path: lower-lying parts of Brixton (around Brixton station, Atlantic Road, and Effra Road) can experience rapid flash surface flooding when storm drains become overwhelmed.
- Major congestion on Brixton Road (A23) and Coldharbour Lane during emergency evacuations.

4. Supplies & Essentials:
- High-street pharmacies, supermarkets, and market grocers along Brixton Road, Atlantic Road, and Electric Avenue carry hydration stocks, staple goods, first-aid materials, and emergency prescriptions.

Note: addresses and opening hours may have changed — confirm on arrival where possible (verify locally).
